about: Permanent plants for tests/support/shuffle-opt-out-scan.ts (#4611 review r1 M2/M3, r2 M-a/M-b, r3 MEDIUM-1). Each entry is a source the gate reads; `accepted` and the four NO-FINDING controls (a harmless string, a type literal, a readable opt-in at a describe, and one bound outside any describe) must be admitted with no finding, every other entry is a spelling of vitest's shuffle suite option that the gate cannot attribute and must red. `expectedReason` is a fragment of the finding's message: without it a branch that reports the same COUNT for the wrong reason (P4 shorthand and P10 accessor were message-only) passes a count-only gate, so deleting a branch that merely rewords a neighbour reds here. The state table this fixture pins is the one in PR #4611 (lane deliverable STATE_TABLE.md; root markdown is gitignored): the reader is an allowlist over parsed object-literal property nodes (oxc-parser), so `harmless-string` and `type-literal` exist to keep the text-census false positive from coming back, `shorthand`, `shorthand-let` and `aliased-*` keep the r2 fail-open closed, and `two-hop-alias*`, `member-alias*`, `spread-before-readable-key` and `readable-opt-in-then-opt-out` keep the r3 one closed: an options object is a SEQUENCE (the effective shuffle value is the last key, no spread and no unnameable key may sit beside it), and a callee resolves through any number of aliases. Data, not a test file: the census scans the tracked tests tree for the option, so a plant written as a .ts file here would red the gate that reads it (and tests/fixtures/** is not collected by vitest either). Keep `expectedFindings` exact: lowering a gate branch without deleting a plant reds the mismatch.

plants.name: accepted
plants.why: the one admitted opt-out spelling: a literal options object holding only the bare shuffle key, set to false, passed directly to a live describe

plants.name: harmless-string
plants.why: the r1 census read string CONTENTS as code, so an option-shaped string in an unrelated file red the gate (#4611 review r2 M-b, Greptile P2); a string is not a property node
plants.source:
const harmless = "{ shuffle: false }";
export const harmlessLength = harmless.length;

plants.name: type-literal
plants.why: a TypeScript type member named shuffle is not a runtime option and must not red (#4611 review r2 M-b); only object literals carry options
plants.source:
type Options = { shuffle: boolean };
export type { Options };

plants.name: literal-true-opt-in
plants.why: STATE_TABLE P2: an explicit shuffle OPT-IN is a readable value and the opposite of an exemption, so it needs no registry row and no finding
plants.source:
import { describe } from "vitest";

describe("plant opt-in", { shuffle: true }, () => {});

plants.name: opt-in-elsewhere
plants.why: STATE_TABLE P2/F1: a readable shuffle opt-in needs no registry row even when its object literal is bound outside any describe, so the net must read the value, not only the key
plants.source: export const SUITE_OPTIONS = { shuffle: true };

plants.name: quoted-key
plants.why: a quoted key is honoured by vitest and invisible to a scanner that blanks string contents (#4611 review r1 M2); the property read names it
plants.expectedReason: spelled as a quoted or computed key
plants.source:
import { describe } from "vitest";

describe("plant quoted", { "shuffle": false }, () => {});

plants.name: computed-key
plants.why: a computed key is honoured by vitest and reads as no key at all to a text-only scanner (#4611 review r1 M2)
plants.expectedReason: spelled as a quoted or computed key
plants.source:
import { describe } from "vitest";

describe("plant computed", { ["shuffle"]: false }, () => {});

plants.name: computed-key-from-variable
plants.why: a computed key whose name is a value: no property-position text spells the option, so only a structural read can see it
plants.expectedReason: computed key whose name this reader cannot resolve

plants.name: unreadable-value
plants.why: STATE_TABLE P3: a shuffle value read from a binding is neither a literal true nor false, so whether the suite opts out cannot be attributed

plants.name: accessor
plants.why: STATE_TABLE P10: an accessor named shuffle is not a value this reader can read, so it must refuse rather than pass as an unknown property
plants.expectedReason: its shuffle property is an accessor

plants.name: shorthand
plants.why: STATE_TABLE P4, the r2 fail-open: `{ shuffle }` passes the binding as the value, and a text census that requires a colon sees no key at all (#4611 review r2 M-a)

plants.name: shorthand-let
plants.why: STATE_TABLE P4: the fail-open is the property FORM, not the binding kind, so a `let` binding reds exactly like the `const` one (#4611 review r2 M-a)

plants.name: shorthand-in-test-options
plants.why: STATE_TABLE F1: the same shorthand in a test's options object is not attributable to a suite at all, and the net reads it wherever the literal sits (#4611 review r2 M-a)

plants.name: aliased-callee
plants.why: STATE_TABLE C3/D2: `const d = describe` rebinds the callee, so a per-file read cannot tie the opt-out to a live registered declaration (#4611 review r2 M-a)
plants.source:
const d = describe;

d("plant aliased", { shuffle: false }, () => {});

plants.name: aliased-computed-key
plants.why: STATE_TABLE C3/P7: an aliased callee plus a computed key is the second r2 fail-open, and the alias is resolved only far enough to refuse it (#4611 review r2 M-a)
plants.expectedReason: computed key whose name this reader cannot resolve

plants.name: bound-in-support-module
plants.why: an options object bound in a non-test module was never read at all: scanning .test.ts files only left it green (#4611 review r1 M2)
plants.source:
/** A shared suite-options object, as a support module might export one. */
export const SUITE_OPTIONS = { shuffle: false };

plants.name: options-imported
plants.why: the use site names the options through an identifier, so a per-file read of the describe call sees nothing (#4611 review r1 M2); the refusal is per call

plants.name: cast-options
plants.why: STATE_TABLE B4: `{ shuffle: false } as const` is not a plain options object argument, so the opt-out inside it is unattributable (#4611 review r2 probe 14)
plants.source:
import { describe } from "vitest";

describe("plant cast", { shuffle: false } as const, () => {});

plants.name: spread-options
plants.why: a describe that spreads another object can carry the opt-out from anywhere; neither the spread site nor its source is attributable

plants.name: spread-beside-opting-out
plants.why: STATE_TABLE P8: a spread beside a literal shuffle key makes the effective options object unreadable, so which value wins cannot be attributed

plants.name: other-options-beside
plants.why: STATE_TABLE P9: an opt-out is admitted only as the minimal `{ shuffle: false }` marker, so an exemption never hides inside a larger options object
plants.source:
import { describe } from "vitest";

describe("plant extra options", { timeout: 5000, shuffle: false }, () => {});

plants.name: unparseable
plants.why: STATE_TABLE H1: a file the parser rejects has no readable options object at all, so it must red with the parse error instead of passing as a file with no opt-out
plants.source:
import { describe } from "vitest";

describe("plant unparseable", { shuffle: false }, () => {};

plants.name: wrapped-in-skip
plants.why: a registered describe inside a skipped suite keeps its registry row valid while the run includes none of it (#4611 review r1 LOW-4)

plants.name: two-hop-alias
plants.why: r3 MEDIUM-1 (Greptile P2 r4307007027): the options are bound to a literal whose SPREAD carries a computed shuffle:false, and the callee is a two-hop alias; vitest evaluates the literal to shuffle:false while r2 read `shuffle: true` and stopped

plants.name: two-hop-alias-inline-literal
plants.why: r3 rule 2: the hidden override sits inline behind a two-hop alias, so the options object itself carries a spread the reader must refuse whatever the callee resolves to

plants.name: member-alias-inline-literal
plants.why: r3 rule 2: a member-expression alias (`const d = V.describe`) is the same defect as an identifier alias, so the binding resolves through the namespace's property name

plants.name: spread-before-readable-key
plants.why: r3 rule 1, the other order: the readable `shuffle: true` comes AFTER the spread, so a reader that stops at its first readable key still fails open on a callee it does not know
plants.source:
const KEY = "shuffle";
later("hidden", { ...{ [KEY]: false }, shuffle: true }, () => {});

plants.name: readable-opt-in-then-opt-out
plants.why: r3 rule 1, last key wins: the literal sets shuffle twice and the LAST value is false, so the effective value is an opt-out wherever the object is used
plants.source: export const SUITE_OPTIONS = { shuffle: true, shuffle: false };

plants.name: unresolved-callee-options
plants.why: r3 rule 2: the callee is a binding this reader cannot follow to a test callee and the call passes an options object, so the opt-out is unattributable rather than ignored
plants.expectedReason: cannot follow to a test callee
plants.source:
const s = wrap(describe);
s("hidden", { shuffle: false }, () => {});

plants.name: unresolved-callee-bound-options
plants.why: r3 rule 2, the bound spelling: the options are a name this file binds to an object literal, so the second argument is options-shaped, while the callee binding the reader cannot follow makes the opt-out unattributable
plants.expectedReason: cannot follow to a test callee
